translation_en: Musaddad narrated to us: Yahya narrated to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, who said: Nafi‘ informed me, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had a man and a woman from the Ansar invoke curses upon one another, and he separated them.

Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us: Malik narrated to us, saying: Nafi‘ narrated to me, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had a man and his wife invoke curses upon one another. The man disavowed the child, so the Prophet separated them and attributed the child to the woman.

Isma‘il narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to me, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, who said: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim informed me, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: The two spouses who invoke curses were mentioned in the presence of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. ‘Asim ibn ‘Adi made a comment about it and then left. A man from his people came to him and told him that he had found another man with his wife. ‘Asim said, ‘I have only been tested with this matter because of what I said.’ He took him to the Messenger of Allah and told him what he had found his wife doing. The man was yellow-complexioned, lean, and straight-haired, while the man he said he had found with his wife was dark-skinned, broad-bodied, heavyset, and tightly curled-haired. The Messenger of Allah said, ‘O Allah, make it clear.’ The woman gave birth resembling the man her husband said he had found with her, so the Messenger of Allah had them invoke curses upon one another. A man in the gathering said to Ibn ‘Abbas, ‘Is she the woman about whom the Messenger of Allah said, “If I were to stone anyone without proof, I would stone her”?’ Ibn ‘Abbas said, ‘No. That was a woman who openly displayed wrongdoing in Islam.’

‘Amr ibn ‘Ali narrated to us: Yahya narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from ‘A’ishah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. ‘Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: ‘Abdah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that Rifa‘ah al-Qurazi married a woman and then divorced her. She married another man and came to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. She told him that the man did not come to her and had only something like a fringe. He said, ‘No, not until you have tasted his sweetness and he has tasted yours.’

Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us: Al-Layth narrated to us, from Ja‘far ibn Rabi‘ah, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz al-A‘raj, who said: Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman informed me that Zaynab bint Abi Salamah told him, from her mother, Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, that a woman from Aslam called Subay‘ah was married to a man who died while she was pregnant. Abu al-Sanabil ibn Ba‘kak proposed to her, but she refused to marry him. He said, ‘By Allah, it is not lawful for you to marry until you have completed the longer of the two waiting periods.’ She remained for nearly ten nights, then came to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said, ‘Marry.’

Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us, from al-Layth, from Yazid, that Ibn Shihab wrote to him that ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah informed him, from his father, who wrote to Ibn al-Arqam asking him to ask Subay‘ah al-Aslamiyyah what ruling the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had given her. She said, ‘He ruled that when I gave birth, I could marry.’

Yahya ibn Qaza‘ah narrated to us: Malik narrated to us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, that Subay‘ah al-Aslamiyyah gave birth a few nights after her husband died. She came to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and asked his permission to marry, and he gave her permission. So she married.

Isma‘il narrated to us: Malik narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, who heard him mention that Yahya ibn Sa‘id ibn al-‘As divorced the daughter of ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hakam, and ‘Abd al-Rahman moved her out of her home. ‘A’ishah, Mother of the Believers, sent word to Marwan, who was governor of Madinah, saying, ‘Fear Allah and return her to her home.’ In Sulayman’s report Marwan said, ‘‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hakam overpowered me.’ Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad said, ‘Has the case of Fatimah bint Qays not reached you?’ She said, ‘It will not harm you not to mention Fatimah’s report.’ Marwan ibn al-Hakam said, ‘If there is evil in you, the evil between these two is enough for you.’

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Ghundar narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, who said: ‘What is the matter with Fatimah? Should she not fear Allah?’—meaning concerning her statement that there is no housing and no maintenance.

‘Amr ibn ‘Abbas narrated to us: Ibn Mahdi narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, who said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr said to ‘A’ishah, ‘Have you seen so-and-so, the daughter of al-Hakam? Her husband divorced her conclusively, and she left.’ She said, ‘How badly she acted.’ He said, ‘Have you not heard what Fatimah said?’ She said, ‘She has no good in mentioning that report.’ Ibn Abi al-Zinad added, from Hisham, from his father: ‘A’ishah strongly criticized her and said, “Fatimah was in a lonely place, and her safety was feared. For that reason the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, granted her that allowance.”’
Hibban narrated to me: ‘Abd Allah informed us: Ibn Jurayj informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Urwah, that ‘A’ishah rejected that view of Fatimah.

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, wanted to depart, he found Safiyyah standing by the entrance of her tent, looking sad. He said to her, ‘May you be bereaved—or may your head be shaven!—you are holding us back. Did you perform the circumambulation of departure on the Day of Sacrifice?’ She said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘Then set out.’
Muhammad narrated to me: ‘Abd al-Wahhab informed us: Yunus narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: Ma‘qil married off his sister, and her husband divorced her once.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me: ‘Abd al-A‘la narrated to us: Sa‘id narrated to us, from Qatadah: Al-Hasan narrated to us that Ma‘qil ibn Yasar’s sister was married to a man who divorced her and left her until her waiting period ended. Then he proposed to her again. Ma‘qil’s pride was stirred by this, and he said, ‘He left her while he had the right to her, then he proposes to her again?’ So he prevented them from marrying. Then Allah revealed, ‘When you divorce women and they reach the end of their waiting period, do not prevent them…’ (2:232), through the end of the verse. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, called Ma‘qil and recited it to him. Ma‘qil gave up his pride and submitted to Allah’s command.

Qutaybah narrated to us: Al-Layth narrated to us, from Nafi‘, that ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with them both, divorced one of his wives once while she was menstruating. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, ordered him to take her back and keep her until she became pure, then menstruated again while with him, then wait until she became pure from that menstruation. If he then wanted to divorce her, he should do so when she was pure and before he had intercourse with her. That is the waiting period during which Allah commanded women to be divorced. When ‘Abd Allah was asked about this, he would tell a man, ‘If you have divorced her three times, she is forbidden to you until she marries another husband.’ Another narrator added from al-Layth: Nafi‘ said that Ibn ‘Umar would say, ‘If you had divorced her once or twice, the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, instructed me about what to do.’

Hajjaj narrated to us: Yazid ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Sirin narrated to us: Yunus ibn Jubayr narrated to me, saying: I asked Ibn ‘Umar. He said, ‘Ibn ‘Umar divorced his wife while she was menstruating. ‘Umar asked the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and he ordered him to take her back, then divorce her before her waiting period began.’ I asked, ‘Does he count that divorce as part of her waiting period?’ He said, ‘What do you think? If he were incapable and foolish?’

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us: Malik informed us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn Hazm, from Humayd ibn Nafi‘, from Zaynab bint Abi Salamah, who informed him of these three reports. Zaynab said: I visited Umm Habibah, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, when her father Abu Sufyan ibn Harb died. Umm Habibah called for perfume containing yellow khaluq or something else, applied some to a servant girl, and then touched her own cheeks with it. She said, ‘By Allah, I have no need for perfume, except that I heard the Messenger of Allah say, “It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn for a dead person for more than three nights, except for her husband: four months and ten days.”’

Zaynab said: I visited Zaynab bint Jahsh when her brother died. She called for perfume and applied some of it. Then she said, ‘By Allah, I have no need for perfume, except that I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say from the pulpit, “It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn for a dead person for more than three nights, except for her husband: four months and ten days.”’

Zaynab said: I heard Umm Salamah say: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, my daughter’s husband has died, and her eyes are troubling her. May she use kohl?’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘No.’ She asked two or three times, and each time he said, ‘No.’ Then the Messenger of Allah said, ‘It is only four months and ten days. In the pre-Islamic period, one of you would throw a piece of dung at the end of a year.’

Humayd said: I asked Zaynab, ‘What does it mean that she threw a piece of dung at the end of a year?’ Zaynab said: When a woman’s husband died, she would enter a small, cramped hut, wear her worst clothes, and use no perfume until a year had passed. Then a donkey, sheep, or bird would be brought to her, and she would rub herself with it. Scarcely would she rub herself with anything without it dying. Then she would come out and be given a piece of dung to throw, after which she could use whatever perfume or other things she wished. Malik was asked what ‘rub herself with it’ meant. He said, ‘She would rub it on her skin.’

Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us: Humayd ibn Nafi‘ narrated to us, from Zaynab bint Umm Salamah, from her mother, that a woman’s husband died and they feared for her eyes. They came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and asked permission for her to use kohl. He said, ‘No. One of you used to stay in the worst of her homes or huts, and when a year had passed and a dog went by, she would throw a piece of dung. No, she must wait until four months and ten days have passed.’

I heard Zaynab bint Umm Salamah narrate from Umm Habibah that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘It is not lawful for a Muslim woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn for more than three days, except for her husband: four months and ten days.’

Musaddad narrated to us: Bishr narrated to us: Salamah ibn ‘Alqamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: Umm ‘Atiyyah said: We were forbidden to mourn for a dead person for more than three days, except for a husband.

‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhab narrated to me: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Hafsah, from Umm ‘Atiyyah, who said: We were forbidden to mourn for a dead person for more than three days, except for a husband: four months and ten days. We were also forbidden to use kohl, perfume, and dyed clothing, except a garment dyed with ‘asb. We were permitted, at the end of our menstrual period after one of us had bathed, to use a small amount of kust and azfar. We were forbidden to follow funeral processions.

Al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Salam ibn Harb narrated to us, from Hisham, from Hafsah, from Umm ‘Atiyyah, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn for more than three days, except for her husband. She must not use kohl or wear dyed clothing, except a garment dyed with ‘asb.’

Al-Ansari said: Hisham narrated to us: Hafsah narrated to us: Umm ‘Atiyyah narrated to me that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, forbade her to use perfume, except a little kust and azfar at the end of her period when she had become pure. Abu ‘Abd Allah said: Kust is like kafur, and azfar is like kafur.

Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me: Rawh ibn ‘Ubadah informed us: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the verse, ‘Those among you who die and leave wives…’ (2:234). He said: A widow was required to observe her waiting period at her husband’s family’s home. Then Allah revealed, ‘Those among you who die and leave wives: a bequest for their wives of maintenance for a year without expelling them. If they leave, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in a fair manner’ (2:240). Allah made a full year for her: seven months and 27 nights as a bequest. If she wished, she could remain in the home provided for her; if she wished, she could leave. That is what Allah means by, ‘without expelling them. If they leave, there is no blame upon you.’ The waiting period remains as it is, and it is obligatory for her. Mujahid held this view. ‘Ata’ said that Ibn ‘Abbas said: This verse abrogated the requirement that she observe her waiting period at her husband’s family’s home; she could observe it wherever she wished. This is what Allah means by, ‘without expelling them.’ ‘Ata’ said: If she wished, she could observe her waiting period at her husband’s family’s home and live in the home bequeathed to her; if she wished, she could leave, because Allah said, ‘There is no blame upon you for what they do.’ ‘Ata’ said: Then the inheritance ruling came and abrogated the right to housing. She could observe her waiting period wherever she wished, and she had no right to housing.

Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us, from Sufyan, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn ‘Amr ibn Hazm. Humayd ibn Nafi‘ narrated to me, from Zaynab bint Umm Salamah, from Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan: When news of her father’s death reached her, she called for perfume, rubbed it on her forearms, and said, ‘I have no need for perfume. Were it not that I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say, “It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn for a dead person for more than three days, except for her husband: four months and ten days,” I would not have used it.’

‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Bakr ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Mas‘ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, forbade the price of a dog, the payment received by a soothsayer, and the bride-price earned by a prostitute.

Adam narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us: ‘Awn ibn Abi Juhaifah narrated to us, from his father, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, cursed the woman who tattoos and the woman who has herself tattooed, those who consume usury and those who pay it, forbade the price of a dog and the earnings of a prostitute, and cursed image-makers.
